title: Data Structures & Algorithms (C++)
scope_in: Coding-interview algorithm problems solved in C++20: arrays, strings, hashing, trees, graphs, DP, greedy, heaps, intervals, bit tricks, number theory; complexity analysis; STL pitfalls.
scope_out: System design (prep-hld/prep-lld), language trivia unrelated to solving problems, non-C++ solutions (translate on request but judge only C++).

modes.output: one verified problem; judge the user's C++ against the harness
rapid conceptual questions (complexity, invariants, STL behaviour), each checked by a runnable snippet when behavioural
concise explanation: invariant, template code in C++, when it fails, 2 canonical problems
resurface due/failed items from memory (spaced repetition), re-judge a fresh attempt
interviewer simulation: statement only, clarifying questions answered tersely, time tracked, full debrief at end

ladder: Warm-up, one idea: Two Sum, Valid Parentheses, Reverse Linked List, Best Time to Buy/Sell Stock.
Standard screen: sliding window (fixed/variable), BFS on grid, binary search on sorted array, prefix sums, hash-map counting, simple tree DFS.
On-site medium: LRU cache, topological sort, binary search on answer, 2D/knapsack DP, union-find, monotonic stack, Dijkstra on small graphs.
Strong on-site / top firm: segment tree or Fenwick, bitmask DP, DP optimisation, trie+DFS, graph with state (BFS on states), tricky greedy with proof.
Elite: Codeforces ~1900-2300 style, multi-insight (offline queries, divide and conquer, SCC/bridges, convex-hull trick, heavy edge-case design).

flaws.F-NO-PLAN: Started coding before restating the problem / working an example / choosing an approach.
flaws.F-BRUTE-SKIPPED: Did not state a brute force and its complexity before optimising.
flaws.F-WRONG-PATTERN: Chose a technique that does not fit the constraints or structure.
flaws.F-GREEDY-UNPROVEN: Greedy choice without exchange argument or counter-example search.
flaws.F-COMPLEXITY-NOT-ANALYSED: Did not state time/space complexity or got it wrong.
flaws.F-EDGE-CASE: Failed an empty/single/extreme input (harness-detected on edge or n<=1 case).
flaws.F-OFF-BY-ONE: Boundary/index off by one (loop bounds, half-open ranges).
flaws.F-STATE-NOT-RESET: Global or loop state carried across test cases / iterations.
flaws.F-WA-LOGIC: Wrong answer from a logic error (harness-detected).
flaws.F-TLE-COMPLEXITY: Correct but too slow at max constraints (harness-detected).
flaws.F-INT-OVERFLOW: int overflow where long long needed (UBSan-detected).
flaws.F-LIFETIME: Use-after-free / dangling reference (e.g. invalidated iterator or reference).
flaws.F-RECURSION-DEPTH: Stack overflow from deep recursion (needs iteration or explicit stack).
flaws.F-STL-MISUSE: STL pitfall: map::operator[] inserting, erase-while-iterating, comparator not strict weak order, vector<bool> quirks.
flaws.F-DEBUG-FLAIL: Changed code at random after a failure instead of reproducing on a minimal case.

x_fields.pattern_chosen: Technique the user first attempted, if different.
x_fields.complexity_claimed: User's stated time/space, e.g. 'O(n log n) / O(n)'.
x_fields.complexity_actual: Actual complexity of their final solution.
x_fields.brute_to_optimal: One line: how (or whether) they moved from brute force to the optimal idea.
x_fields.verdict: Harness verdict of final submission: AC/WA/TLE/RE/SAN/CE.
x_fields.attempts: Number of submissions before AC or give-up.

items_note: the whole problem dir: statement.md, ref/brute/gen/edge/meta, plus the user's last solution
rubric_body:
## Verdict-driven (the harness decides correctness; never judge by reading)

| Dimension | Evidence |
|-----------|----------|
| Correctness | `judge.py judge` verdict AC (also passes ASan/UBSan) |
| Efficiency | passes large cases within `tl_s`; stated complexity matches `complexity_actual` |
| Process | restated problem, worked an example, named brute force then optimised, tested edge cases before submitting |
| Code quality | readable, no UB warnings, sensible STL use |

Process flaws (F-NO-PLAN, F-BRUTE-SKIPPED, F-COMPLEXITY-NOT-ANALYSED, F-DEBUG-FLAIL) are judged from the conversation transcript and logged even when the verdict is AC.
outcome_rule:
- **pass**: verdict AC AND ≤1 hint (tier ≤2) AND stated complexity correct.
- **partial**: AC with a tier ≥3 hint or wrong/missing complexity analysis, OR a correct-but-slow solution (TLE) with the right idea.
- **fail**: WA/RE/SAN/CE not fixed by session end, wrong approach, or gave up.
loop_extra:
### DSA specifics
All paths relative to this skill's directory. Work in the scratchpad, e.g. `P=<scratchpad>/dsa/<ref>`.
1. **Generate** — write `$P/{statement.md,ref.cpp,brute.cpp,gen.cpp,edge/*.in,meta.json}` per `harness/judge.py` docstring. `gen.cpp <seed> <n>` must be deterministic; use tiny value ranges on small cases to force ties/negatives and full range on large cases. Choose `large_n`/`tl_s` so the intended solution passes and the brute force does not.
2. **Verify** — `python3 harness/judge.py verify $P`. Exit 0 required (it checks ref==brute on edge+200 small cases under sanitizers, ref speed, and that brute fails the limit). On failure read `stage`/`detail`, fix, retry (max 3), else tell the user and fall back to a different problem. Pass `--allow-fast-brute` only at level 1.
3. **Present** — print `statement.md` only (plus time box if `--timed`: L1 15m, L2 25m, L3 35m, L4 45m, L5 60m).
4. **Interact** — before accepting code, ask once (unprompted only if they jump straight to code): approach + complexity. When the user submits code, save to `$P/sol.cpp` and run `python3 harness/judge.py judge $P $P/sol.cpp`. Report verdict + `case` + the minimal failing `input` + `flaws`; do NOT reveal the reference solution. Resubmissions count as `attempts`.
5. **Debrief** — show a clean reference approach (from `ref.cpp`), the key insight, and map every harness `flaws` entry plus process flaws to taxonomy codes.
6. **Remember** — `save-item` the whole `$P` (exclude `.build`), then `append` with `x` per schema.

**Quiz/explain** items about behaviour (complexity, iterator invalidation, UB) must be confirmed by compiling and running a tiny C++ snippet before they are asked.
**Mock**: no hints unless the user asks; clarify requirements tersely like an interviewer; evaluate both process and code; fan-out generation for the n problems may use parallel subagents.
gate_extra: Harness is mandatory: `python3 harness/judge.py verify <dir>` must exit 0 before the statement is shown. `python3 harness/judge.py selftest` proves the harness itself (run it if a verdict looks suspicious).
Language is C++20 (`g++ -std=c++20 -O2`); the same solution is also built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined` — UB that 'works' still counts as a flaw.
Dedupe: skip any `item.ref` already in memory (`MEM seen dsa <ref>`) unless in review mode; refs follow `dsa-<topic>-<slug>`.
